typeName: Rate in context from a table
title: Oil pumped into a tanker truck

stimulus.title: Oil pumped into a tanker truck
stimulus.html:
Oil is pumped into a tanker truck at a rate R(t)R(t) gallons per minute, where tt is measured in minutes. RR is differentiable and increasing on 0≤t≤120 \le t \le 12. Selected values of R(t)R(t) are shown in the table.
Rate R(t), in gallons per minute, at selected times t, in minutes
tt (minutes)035912
R(t)R(t) (gallons per minute)1218212930

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Use the data in the table to estimate R′(4)R'(4). Show the computations that lead to your answer. Indicate units of measure.

rubric.point: A difference quotient using <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 3</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 5</annotation></semantics></math>

Answer <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> gallons per minute per minute

parts.sample: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R'(4)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>≈</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx \frac{R(5) - R(3)}{5 - 3}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>21</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>18</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{21 - 18}{2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1.5</annotation></semantics></math> gallons per minute per minute.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Use a trapezoidal sum with the four subintervals indicated by the data in the table to approximate ∫012R(t)dt\int_0^{12} R(t)\,dt. Show the computations that lead to your answer.

rubric.point: A trapezoidal sum with the table's four widths 3, 2, 4 and 3

parts.sample: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>12</mn></msubsup><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^{12} R(t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>≈</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>12</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>18</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>18</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>21</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>21</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>29</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>29</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 3 \cdot \frac{12 + 18}{2} + 2 \cdot \frac{18 + 21}{2} + 4 \cdot \frac{21 + 29}{2} + 3 \cdot \frac{29 + 30}{2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>45</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>39</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>88.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 45 + 39 + 100 + 88.5</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>272.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 272.5</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Using correct units, explain the meaning of ∫012R(t)dt\int_0^{12} R(t)\,dt in the context of the problem.

rubric.point: The number of gallons of oil pumped into the truck from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 12</annotation></semantics></math> minutes
accept: must name the quantity (gallons of oil pumped in), the units (gallons) and the interval (0 to 12 minutes)

parts.sample: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>12</mn></msubsup><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^{12} R(t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math> is the total number of gallons of oil pumped into the tanker truck from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 12</annotation></semantics></math> minutes.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: A left Riemann sum with the four subintervals indicated by the table is used to approximate ∫012R(t)dt\int_0^{12} R(t)\,dt. Find its value, and explain whether it is an overestimate or an underestimate.

accept: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>12</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>18</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>21</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>29</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3(12) + 2(18) + 4(21) + 3(29)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>243</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 243</annotation></semantics></math>

rubric.point: Underestimate, because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> is increasing on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>12</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 12]</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: must name R (or the rate) as increasing; "the graph goes up" alone earns nothing

parts.sample: Left sum <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>12</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>18</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>21</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>29</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 3(12) + 2(18) + 4(21) + 3(29)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>243</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 243</annotation></semantics></math>. Because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> is increasing on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>12</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 12]</annotation></semantics></math>, on each subinterval <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> is least at the left end, so each rectangle lies under the graph: 243 is an underestimate.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: Must there be a value tt, with 5<t<95 < t < 9, for which R′(t)=2R'(t) = 2? Justify your answer.

rubric.point: Computes <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{R(9) - R(5)}{9 - 5}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>29</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>21</mn></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{29 - 21}{4}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: the average rate of change over [5, 9] equals 2

rubric.point: Concludes yes by the Mean Value Theorem, stating that <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> is differentiable (so continuous) on the interval
accept: "<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> is differentiable, so it is continuous on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[5, 9]</annotation></semantics></math> and differentiable on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(5, 9)</annotation></semantics></math>; by the MVT ..."

parts.sample: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> is differentiable, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> is continuous on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[5, 9]</annotation></semantics></math> and differentiable on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(5, 9)</annotation></semantics></math>. <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{R(9) - R(5)}{9 - 5}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>29</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>21</mn></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{29 - 21}{4}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2</annotation></semantics></math>. By the Mean Value Theorem, there is a value <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo><</mo><mi>t</mi><mo><</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5 < t < 9</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R'(t) = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.
